en: to be docile; to be tractable

examples.en: The job market is not easy these days.

examples.ko: 서울에서 혼자 사는 일이 녹록지 않았어요.
examples.en: Living alone in Seoul wasn't easy.
If you take that team lightly, you will get burned.

examples.ko: 처음 하는 장사가 녹록할 리가 없지요.
examples.en: A first-time business can't possibly be easy.

examples.ko: 요즘 경기가 나빠서 장사가 녹록지 않다고 해요.
examples.en: They say business isn't easy because the economy is bad these days.

examples.ko: 세상살이는 녹록한 게 아니라고 어머니가 늘 말씀하세요.
examples.en: My mother always says that life in this world is not a pushover.

explain: '녹록하지 않다'처럼 부정 표현과 함께 써서 '쉽지 않다, 만만치 않다'라는 뜻으로 말하는 경우가 많아요. 줄이면 '녹록지 않다'가 맞는 표기예요. 상황이나 사람이 만만하다는 뜻이라 사람에게 쓰면 '순해서 다루기 쉬운'이라는 뜻이 되기도 해요.

phrases.en: Making ends meet is not easy these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '녹록하지 않아요'의 줄임말로, 상황이 만만하지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A contracted form of '녹록하지 않아요', used when a situation is not easy.

phrases.example: 녹록하지 않은 현실이지만 포기하지 않을 거예요.
phrases.en: It is a tough reality, but I won't give up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 명사를 붙여 '쉽지 않은 ~'라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attached before a noun to mean 'a not-easy ~'.

phrases.en: Life studying abroad was not easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일이 쉽지 않았다고 말할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past tense, used to say that something was not easy.

explain_en: It is often used with a negative, as in '녹록하지 않다', to mean 'not easy' or 'not a pushover'. The correct shortened spelling is '녹록지 않다'. It describes a situation or person as easy to handle, and said of a person it can mean 'meek and easy to deal with'.

examples.ko: 그는 본업이 의사이고 취미로 노래를 해요.
examples.en: His main job is doctor, and he sings as a hobby.
These days my side job is busier than my main job.
I couldn't rest because I focused on my main job.
Singing is his main job, but he also acts.
I quit my main job and opened a shop.
It's hard to do my main job and child care together.

explain: 본업은 부업과 짝으로 쓰는 말이고, 가장 중심이 되는 직업이에요. 학생에게는 '본분'이라는 말을 써서 공부가 본분이라고 해요. 직업을 물을 때는 '본업이 뭐예요?'보다 '무슨 일을 하세요?'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I'm busy because I do both my main job and a side job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝말인 '부업'과 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, paired with '부업'.

phrases.example: 그는 본업이 따로 있고 주말에만 가수로 일해요.
phrases.en: He has a main job elsewhere and sings only on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주로 하는 일이 다른 곳에 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say one's main work is something else.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a separate main job

phrases.en: I want to focus on my main job now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 일보다 중심이 되는 일에 힘쓴다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means putting effort into the central job over other things.
phrases.en_equiv: to focus on one's main job

explain_en: 본업 pairs with 부업 (side job) and means the central occupation. For students people use 본분, saying that studying is their 본분. When asking someone's job, 무슨 일을 하세요? sounds more natural than 본업이 뭐예요?

examples.en: A good environment helps a child grow.
That experience made me grow.
I want to grow the company big.
I am looking for ways to develop my skills.
Sunlight is important for growing plants.
They grew a small shop into a chain.

explain: '자라다'는 스스로 크는 것이고 '성장시키다'는 누군가가 키우거나 발전시키는 것이에요. 회사, 실력, 경제처럼 추상적인 것에도 써요. 사람이 크는 일은 '키우다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 자라는 일에는 '성장시키다'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For people growing up, this is used more than 성장시키다.

phrases.en: I improve my skills by practicing every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실력이나 기술을 더 좋게 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means making skills or technology better.

phrases.en: A new product makes the company grow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 경제 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation in talk about companies and the economy.

explain_en: The intransitive verb is growing by itself; this one is making something grow or develop. It works for abstract things like a company, skill or economy. For raising children, the plain verb for raising is more common.

dis.h: make a company or person develop and grow

p.n: 재배하다 means growing crops or plants, so it cannot replace this sentence.

en: to end a semester; to finish the course

examples.en: Our class ends next week.
The professor finished the course with today's class.
When the semester ends, the library becomes quiet.
When did your classes end that you're so free?
The day the course ends is different for each subject.
Some lectures ended early.

explain: 반대말은 '개강하다'예요. 주어로 '수업, 강의, 학교, 교수님'이 자연스럽게 와요. 학기의 마지막 수업이 끝났을 때 쓰는 말이라서 하루 수업이 끝나는 것에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.nuance_en: This is the past tense, saying the semester has already ended.

phrases.en: When the semester ends, I'll go home right away.
phrases.nuance_en: With -(으)면 it introduces what happens once the semester ends.

phrases.en: On the last day of class, the teacher gave us snacks.
phrases.nuance_en: -는 modifies 날, which is close to 종강 날.

explain_en: Its opposite is '개강하다'. Natural subjects are a class, a lecture, a school or a professor. It means the last class of the term is over, so it isn't used for a single day's lesson ending.

examples.en: I entered the university this year as a transfer student.

examples.ko: 편입생은 학점 인정 절차를 먼저 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: Transfer students need to check the credit recognition process first.

examples.ko: 우리 반에 편입생이 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are two transfer students in our class.
An information session for transfer students is being held.
My transfer student friend says the school still feels unfamiliar.
Some schools give scholarships to transfer students.

explain: 주로 대학에서 다른 학교나 학과에서 옮겨 온 학생을 말해요. 초·중·고등학교에서는 보통 '전학생'이라고 하고, 처음 입학한 학생은 '신입생'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I transferred to this university last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편입생'이 사람이라면 '편입하다'는 다른 학교에서 옮겨 들어오는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 'transfer student' names the person, this verb describes the act of moving in from another school.

phrases.en: Many departments are recruiting transfer students this year.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in university announcements.

phrases.en: I'm a transfer student who joined this semester.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when introducing yourself and stating your status.

explain_en: It mainly refers to a student who moved into a university from another school or major. In elementary through high school, people usually say '전학생', and a first-time entrant is a '신입생'.
